questions.question: E-Gov vision and e-Gov objectives differ mainly in —

options.A: The domain where they are to be implemented
options.B: The level of authority where the responsibility lies
options.C: The kind of technology to be used
options.D: The group of people who will actually benefit

questions.explanation: A vision statement is a broad, aspirational declaration usually owned and sanctioned at a higher policy/leadership level, whereas the specific objectives that operationalize it are typically set and pursued at the implementing department or project level. This difference in who holds responsibility at what level is what most distinguishes vision from objectives in e-Governance strategy documents, rather than differences in domain, technology, or beneficiary group, which the other three options incorrectly propose as the distinguishing factor.

questions.sub: Categories of Government services (G2C, G2B, G2E, G2G)
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a G2B (Government to Business) service?

options.A: Issuance of business licenses and permits
options.B: Government's internal communication network
options.C: Delivery of healthcare services to citizens
options.D: Voting systems for citizens

questions.explanation: G2B (Government-to-Business) covers government interactions that serve or regulate enterprises, and issuing business licenses/permits is a textbook G2B transaction — a business obtaining a legal authorization from government. Internal communication networks are G2G (government-to-government), healthcare delivery to citizens is G2C, and voting systems serve citizens/G2C as well; none of these three involve a government service consumed specifically by a business entity, which is what defines the G2B category.

questions.sub: Categories of Government services (G2C, G2B, G2E, G2G)
questions.question: Which of the following most probably fall under G2G service?

options.A: Application of new electricity connection by Transport department
options.B: Revenue disbursement to government by electricity department
options.C: Payment of electricity bills by consumers to the department
options.D: Complaints made by Transport department regarding their electricity connection

questions.explanation: G2G (Government-to-Government) describes one government entity/department transacting with another. A Transport department applying to the Electricity department for a new connection is exactly that — one government office requesting a service from a different government office, with no citizen or business involved. Paying electricity bills is G2C/citizen-to-government, and while options B and D also technically involve two government bodies, A is the cleanest, most standard textbook illustration of an inter-departmental government service request.

questions.question: A vision statement is one of the following:

options.A: It is a specific and usually quantifiable statement
options.B: It is generate from business strategy
options.C: It represents a quantification of program goal
options.D: It represents specific conditions and ambitions of the organization

questions.explanation: A vision statement is qualitative and aspirational, describing the conditions and ambitions the organisation wants to reach. It is not quantifiable and does not derive from business strategy, since strategy is formulated to realise the vision, not the other way round.

questions.sub: Categories of Government services (G2C, G2B, G2E, G2G)
questions.question: G2C services include:

options.A: Career enhancement
options.B: Professional Education
options.C: Permits
options.D: Returns

questions.explanation: Permits, along with licences and certificates, are classic Government-to-Citizen transactions. Career enhancement and professional education fall under G2E (employee-facing), while filing of returns is typically classified under G2B taxation services.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Pilot and rollout
questions.question: Which is the least risky implementation process?

options.A: Parallel Adoption
options.B: Phased rollout
options.C: Big Bang
options.D: Pilot and rollout

questions.explanation: Parallel adoption runs the legacy and new systems side by side, so the old system remains a working fallback and errors are caught by comparison, making it the least risky though the most costly. Big Bang, with no fallback, is the riskiest.

questions.sub: Categories of Government services (G2C, G2B, G2E, G2G)
questions.question: Which of the following is not an interaction between main groups in e-Governance?

options.A: G2E
options.B: G2B
options.C: G2G
options.D: C2G

questions.explanation: The four standard e-Governance interaction domains are G2C, G2B, G2G and G2E, all of which are government-initiated. C2G is not part of that canonical set, though some wider taxonomies do describe citizen-to-government flows, which is why the printed list is a little loose.

questions.question: In e-governance planning, what distinguishes the vision from the strategy?

options.A: The vision is prepared by the vendor and the strategy by the department
options.B: The vision lists the applications to be procured and the strategy fixes their delivery dates
options.C: The vision states the desired future state in outcome terms, while the strategy states the choices and the route by which that state will be reached
options.D: The vision is revised every quarter while the strategy stays fixed for the life of the programme

questions.explanation: A vision is a short statement of the end state the government wants for its citizens, deliberately free of implementation detail, while the strategy sets out the deliberate choices, priorities and sequence that will get there. Neither is a procurement list; that belongs further down, in the roadmap and the detailed project report.

questions.question: Within an e-governance strategy document, the 'roadmap' is best described as

options.A: the sequenced, time-bound set of initiatives, with their dependencies, that turns the strategy into a programme of work
options.B: the network topology diagram of the state-wide area network
options.C: the list of hardware and software licences to be purchased in the first year
options.D: the escalation hierarchy used to resolve inter-departmental disputes

questions.explanation: The roadmap converts strategic intent into an ordered schedule of initiatives, showing what is taken up when and what each item depends on. A licence and hardware list is a procurement plan, which is derived from the roadmap rather than being the roadmap itself.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs in an e-governance strategy rather than in implementation-level design?

options.A: The database schema chosen for the citizen registry
options.B: The prioritisation of services for digitisation and the sequence in which they are taken up
options.C: The counter layout of a common service centre
options.D: The naming convention adopted for application servers

questions.explanation: Deciding which services matter most and in what order they will be taken up is a strategic choice about where limited capacity and money go, and it drives everything downstream. Schemas, layouts and naming conventions are design and operational decisions taken once the strategic choices are already settled.

questions.question: In e-governance strategy development, the purpose of a gap analysis is to

options.A: compare the bids received from the shortlisted system integrators
options.B: measure the difference between budgeted and actual expenditure at the close of the year
options.C: check whether the pilot's throughput matches the service levels promised by the vendor
options.D: compare the present state of services, processes, infrastructure and skills with the state the vision demands, so the strategy can close the difference

questions.explanation: Gap analysis is the bridge between the as-is assessment and the vision: it names precisely what is missing in processes, systems, data, capacity and policy, and those gaps become the strategy's initiatives. Comparing bids or budget variance are procurement and financial exercises with no bearing on strategic direction.

questions.question: Which of the following is stated as an outcome-level objective of e-governance rather than as an output?

options.A: Reducing the time and the number of office visits a citizen needs in order to obtain a certificate
options.B: Commissioning a state data centre with a stated uptime
options.C: Issuing digital signature certificates to all sanctioning officers
options.D: Deploying an online application portal in every district office

questions.explanation: An outcome describes the change experienced by the user, such as fewer visits and shorter turnaround, whereas an output is a deliverable the programme produces. Portals, data centres and certificates are outputs, and a programme can deliver all of them while the citizen's experience remains unchanged.

questions.question: Why are e-governance objectives expected to be expressed with a baseline value and a target date?

options.A: Because tender documents cannot be issued until objectives are quantified by the auditor
options.B: Because quantified objectives let the vendor fix the contract price
options.C: Because without a baseline and a target, no one can later establish whether the programme actually delivered the intended benefit
options.D: Because objectives must be quantified before any officer can be assigned to the project

questions.explanation: A baseline records the position before the intervention and the target defines success, so benefit realisation can be evaluated afterwards instead of being asserted. Contract pricing rests on scope and service levels, which are separate artefacts from programme-level objectives.

questions.question: In stakeholder analysis for an e-governance project, stakeholders are conventionally mapped along which two dimensions?

options.A: Seniority in the government hierarchy and total length of service
options.B: Their level of interest in the project and their power to affect it
options.C: Distance of their office from the state headquarters and the population they serve
options.D: Their technical skill and their willingness to attend training

questions.explanation: The power-interest grid sorts stakeholders into those to manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed or merely monitor, which determines how much engagement effort each group receives. Seniority is a poor proxy, because a low-ranking frontline clerk can have very high power to obstruct a system in daily use.

questions.question: When a department compiles its service list for an e-governance strategy, a 'service' is best defined as

options.A: a software module to be delivered by the system integrator
options.B: an internal file or register maintained by the department
options.C: a sanctioned post in the department's staffing pattern
options.D: a distinct transaction or outcome the department delivers to an identified user, such as issuing a licence

questions.explanation: Services are defined from the user's side, as something a citizen, business or another agency asks for and receives, which is what makes prioritisation and service-level setting meaningful. Modules, registers and posts describe the department's internal arrangements and can exist without any user-visible service at all.

questions.question: In an e-governance strategy, a multi-channel delivery approach means that

options.A: the same service is offered through several access points, such as a portal, a mobile application, a service centre and a departmental counter, over a single back-end
options.B: each department runs its own separate portal for its own services
options.C: the service is delivered by several vendors working under separate contracts
options.D: the citizen must use one channel to apply and a different channel to pay

questions.explanation: Multi-channel delivery means one authoritative back-end and one set of rules, reachable through whichever front-end suits the user, so status and records stay consistent across channels. Several departmental portals is fragmentation, which is the problem multi-channel design is meant to solve.

questions.question: Why does a state e-governance strategy normally retain an assisted channel such as a common service centre alongside a self-service portal?

options.A: Because an online application is invalid unless counter-signed at a centre
options.B: Because portals are technically unable to accept payments
options.C: Because citizens without devices, connectivity or digital literacy would otherwise be shut out of the service
options.D: Because an assisted channel costs government less to run than a portal

questions.explanation: Assisted channels exist for inclusion: they let an operator complete the transaction on behalf of a citizen who cannot, which keeps the service universal rather than available only to the connected. Assisted delivery normally costs more per transaction than self-service, so cost is an argument against it, not for it.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Big bang
questions.question: A big-bang implementation approach for a new government system means that

options.A: the system is first released to a small group of volunteer users
options.B: the legacy system is retired and every user moves to the new system on a single cut-over date
options.C: the system is released module by module across several financial years
options.D: the old and the new system both process live work until the new one is trusted

questions.explanation: Big bang is a single, complete changeover on a fixed date, with the old system switched off at that moment. Running both systems on live work is parallel adoption, and releasing module by module is a phased rollout.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Big bang
questions.question: What is the principal risk of a big-bang cut-over in a citizen-facing government service?

options.A: Training costs rise because staff must be trained twice over
options.B: The vendor cannot be held to any service level agreement during cut-over
options.C: Data migration becomes unnecessary, which weakens the audit trail
options.D: There is no fallback, so a serious defect at go-live stops the service everywhere at once

questions.explanation: Because the legacy system is switched off, a big bang concentrates all risk into one moment and leaves nothing to revert to, which is why it suits small or low-criticality systems far better than statewide citizen services. Big bang in fact makes data migration more critical, since the entire legacy dataset must be correct on day one.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Phased rollout
questions.question: In a phased rollout, the phases are most usefully defined by

options.A: a coherent slice of geography, user group or functionality that can go live and be stabilised before the next slice starts
options.B: the financial year in which each instalment of the vendor's payment falls due
options.C: the alphabetical order of the districts to be covered
options.D: the number of servers commissioned in the data centre each quarter

questions.explanation: The value of phasing lies in learning, so each phase must be a self-contained unit that can actually operate and be stabilised, letting its lessons improve the next phase. Slicing by payment schedule or alphabetical order ignores dependencies and delivers phases that cannot stand on their own.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Phased rollout
questions.question: Which of the following is a genuine disadvantage of a phased rollout compared with a single cut-over?

options.A: Defects found in an early phase cannot be corrected before the later phases begin
options.B: Users covered in later phases receive no training at all
options.C: The old and the new arrangements must coexist for longer, adding interface, reconciliation and support effort
options.D: The total number of users who must eventually be migrated increases

questions.explanation: A long transition means two ways of working, sometimes two datasets, and temporary interfaces that must be built, run and later thrown away, which is the real price paid for reduced risk. Correcting defects between phases is the chief benefit of phasing, not a drawback.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Parallel adoption
questions.question: Parallel adoption of a new system means that

options.A: two vendors build competing versions and the better one is retained
options.B: the old and the new system are run simultaneously on the same live workload until the new one is proven, after which the old one is withdrawn
options.C: the system is rolled out to two districts at a time until the whole state is covered
options.D: development and testing teams work at the same time in order to shorten the schedule

questions.explanation: Parallel running keeps the legacy system live and authoritative while the new system processes the same transactions, so the outputs can be compared and the old system remains available as a fallback. Covering two districts at a time is simply a phased rollout with small phases.

questions.sub: Implementation approach and plan: Parallel adoption
questions.question: The main cost of parallel adoption is that

options.A: staff must enter and reconcile the same transactions in both systems, roughly doubling the workload for the duration of the parallel run
options.B: the new system cannot be exercised against real data during the run
options.C: no fallback exists if the new system fails at go-live
options.D: data from the legacy system can no longer be migrated

questions.explanation: Double entry and daily reconciliation impose a heavy, sustained burden on the same frontline staff who are also learning the new system, which is why parallel runs are kept short and are reserved for high-risk services. The absence of a fallback is the defect of a big-bang cut-over, and is precisely what parallel adoption avoids.

questions.question: What distinguishes programme management from project management in a state e-governance initiative?

options.A: Programme management applies only to projects funded by the central government
options.B: A programme coordinates a set of related projects towards a shared outcome and manages their interdependencies, while each project delivers its own defined output
options.C: Programme management is performed by the vendor and project management by the department
options.D: Programme management covers the procurement stage only, and project management everything after it

questions.explanation: A programme exists because several projects, such as infrastructure, applications, capacity building and process re-engineering, must land together before any benefit appears, so its job is interdependency, shared resources and benefit realisation. A project is accountable for its own output on time and budget, whether or not the wider benefit materialises.

questions.question: In an e-governance programme management framework, the role of the programme management unit is chiefly to

options.A: take the final policy decisions on behalf of the department
options.B: write the application code the system integrator fails to deliver on time
options.C: supply the day-to-day coordination, monitoring and technical capacity the department cannot spare, with decisions still resting with the steering committee
options.D: carry out the financial bid evaluation in place of the tender committee

questions.explanation: A programme management unit is a support and assurance structure that tracks progress, manages risk, checks vendor deliverables and gives the department technical depth it lacks in-house. Authority stays with the apex or steering committee, because a support unit that starts taking policy decisions has displaced the accountable department.
